memos.headline: S07 and S09 Lead on Momentum; S04 and S02 in Deep Downtrends — Trend Divergence Widest in Universe
memos.body: I see the clearest trend separation in months across this universe. S07 is the standout leader at 759.74, up 82% over 26 weeks with relative strength vs SPY of +33.4% over 12 weeks, though it sits 17.4% above its 50d mean and RSI at 66.9 warns of near-term extension — I'd wait for a pullback toward the 50d before adding, and a close below ~650 (roughly the 50d area) would change my view. S09 is the second-best trend with +37.2% over 26 weeks and +21.2% relative strength over 12 weeks, 12% above its 50d mean and only 5.3% off highs, but RSI at 58.7 is more comfortable than S07. On the other side, S04 is deeply broken: RSI 32, down 26.7% from its 52w high, 18.4% below the 200d mean, and bleeding relative strength at -20.5% over 12 weeks — I see no reason to step in front of that until price reclaims the 200d. S02 is similarly ugly with a 51.6% drawdown from highs and -14% relative strength over 12 weeks, though the 1-week bounce of +2% is too thin to call a reversal.

views.note: Dominant uptrend with +82% 26w return and +33.4% 12w relative strength, but 17% above 50d mean creates pullback risk; would reassess below ~650.
Strong trend with +37.2% 26w gain, +21.2% 12w relative strength, RSI 58.7 not yet overbought; a break below ~131 (near 50d) would change my view.
RSI 32, -26.7% drawdown, 18.4% below 200d mean, and -20.5% 12w relative strength — textbook downtrend with no sign of stabilization.
Massive 51.6% drawdown from highs, 8.8% below both 50d and 200d means, and -18.3% 4w relative strength; would need a sustained reclaim of the 200d to reconsider.
Quiet uptrend with +7.2% 4w return, +8.3% above 50d, low ATR of 1.98%, and positive relative strength; RSI 66.4 approaching overbought so sizing should be modest.
Balanced profile near 50d mean with RSI 49.9 and modest +5.7% 26w return; no strong directional signal either way.
Down 17.3% from highs, 8.1% below 50d, RSI 39.3, and -9.4% 12w relative strength; the +5.3% weekly bounce is encouraging but insufficient to call a reversal.

memos.headline: S10 and S04 Deliver Exceptional Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Show Cash-Flow Compression
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable high-margin growers and names where earnings are deteriorating despite revenue holding up. S10 stands out with 56% net margins, +62.5% YoY revenue growth, and minimal debt of $8.47B — the strongest fundamental profile in the group. S04 is similarly compelling at 47.3% net margins with net income up 59.5% YoY on $81.27B of revenue. On the other end, S02's net margin has collapsed to 2.1% with net income down 61.2% YoY despite 12.2% revenue growth, signaling severe cost or mix headwinds, and S09 posted a -1.3% revenue decline alongside a -14.6% net income drop with a thin 7.9% margin. I would need to see margin stabilization in S02 and a return to positive revenue growth in S09 before reconsidering either name.

views.note: 56% net margin, 62.5% YoY revenue growth, and only $8.47B debt make this the best fundamental story in the universe.
47.3% net margin with net income surging 59.5% YoY on 16.7% revenue growth demonstrates exceptional operating leverage.
30.3% net margin, 18% revenue growth, 29.8% net income growth, and low debt of $14.79B reflect durable earnings power.
$143.76B revenue growing 15.7% with 29.3% net margins is solid, though $88.50B in total debt warrants monitoring.
Revenue up 13.6% but net income only +5.9% with a thin 9.9% margin suggests margin pressure is absorbing top-line gains.
28.4% net margin is healthy but net income declined 7% YoY and $435B in total debt (financial entity) limits upside conviction.
Revenue growth of just 1.5% and net income declining 6.7% YoY on a 19.4% margin suggests stalling momentum; need to see reacceleration.
18% revenue growth is encouraging but net income fell 13.9% and 12.5% margin with $36.2B debt signals cost headwinds.
Revenue declining 1.3% with net income down 14.6% and a 7.9% net margin points to deteriorating earnings power.
Net margin collapsed to 2.1% and net income fell 61.2% YoY despite 12.2% revenue growth — severe cash-flow compression.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact With Benign Inflation—Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth and Banks Over Defensives
memos.body: I see a clear mid-cycle easing regime: the fed funds upper bound is at 3.75%, down 75bp over the past year, while CPI is running at just 2.4% YoY—comfortably near target. Unemployment at 4.30% has ticked up 30bp YoY but improved 10bp over the last three months, suggesting the labor market is softening gently rather than cracking. The 10y yield at 4.08% is down 42bp YoY and the 2s10s curve has re-steepened to +61bp, a positive signal for banks and duration assets. I have conviction that this easing/soft-landing backdrop favors growth and financials; a CPI print re-accelerating above 3% or unemployment jumping above 4.6% would force me to revisit the regime call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits directly from falling rates and a benign inflation backdrop.
Banks gain from a steepening yield curve (+36bp YoY in 2s10s) and still-healthy labor market supporting credit quality.
Cyclicals should benefit from easing financial conditions and a labor market that is stabilizing rather than deteriorating.
Staples offer less upside in an easing regime where risk appetite is supported; hold but do not add.
Energy lacks a clear macro tailwind here—neither strong reflation nor deep recession—so I stay on the sideline.
Rate-sensitive sectors broadly favored as the Fed has cut 75bp YoY with more easing likely given tame inflation.
Macro backdrop is not hostile but no strong directional signal for this name from current data.
Defensive positioning is less attractive when the curve is steepening and the Fed is easing into a soft landing.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S02 and S04 Washouts May Be Bottoming While S07 and S01 Ride Positive Momentum
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions across the universe as the primary sentiment signal this cycle. S02 suffered a brutal -19.6% one-day drop on its Jan-27 results and S04 fell -10.0% on Jan-28; both moves are severe enough that negative sentiment is likely fully priced or oversold, creating potential mean-reversion setups if narrative tone stabilizes. On the positive side, S07 posted a clean +3.4% reaction on Jan-29 results and S01 gained +2.6% on Jan-22 earnings, suggesting constructive sentiment that has room to build. S03's -5.6% drop on Feb-05 results is more recent and may still be digesting, while S06's -4.2% Jan-13 reaction followed by a flurry of governance and other-event filings suggests ongoing uncertainty rather than a clean washout.

views.note: A -19.6% earnings-day selloff is extreme and likely overshoots fundamental damage; sentiment washout creates contrarian opportunity if tone stabilizes.
The -10.0% post-earnings drop signals heavy negative sentiment that may already be priced, offering a potential bounce if no further negative catalysts emerge.
A +3.4% positive earnings reaction and governance changes suggest constructive sentiment momentum with no crowding concerns yet.
Solid +2.6% earnings reaction and multiple Reg FD disclosures point to proactive, positive communication that supports sentiment.
A -4.2% earnings reaction followed by director changes and multiple other-event filings signals unresolved uncertainty rather than a clean reset.
The -5.6% earnings drop on Feb-05 is recent enough that negative sentiment may not yet be fully digested.
A muted +0.5% earnings reaction and a director change are low-signal events; no clear sentiment direction.
A +0.6% earnings reaction is essentially flat, indicating balanced sentiment with no strong directional read.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surges to Near-500 While Oil Rallies 12% in a Month — Geopolitical Risk Repricing Underway
memos.body: I am flagging a structural shift in the policy uncertainty backdrop: the EPU index has more than doubled over three months to 493.80, a level historically associated with major trade-policy or sanctions escalations. WTI crude at $66.66 is up 12.2% month-over-month and 10.6% over three months, consistent with supply-side tightening or energy-security concerns rather than demand-driven moves, given that HY spreads have widened 23 bps in the last month. VIX at 20.23 is elevated but not panicked, suggesting markets are pricing incremental policy risk rather than a full-blown crisis. Without specific GDELT event detail, the 8-K filings across S01, S02, S06, and S09 (all Reg FD disclosures in January) may reflect companies proactively communicating exposure to new export controls or tariff actions; S06's three filings in five weeks are particularly notable. My base case is that energy-exposed and domestically-oriented names benefit, while companies with concentrated China or cross-border supply chains face headwinds until policy clarity improves — a reversal of tariff actions or a sanctions de-escalation would change my view.

views.note: Three 8-K filings in five weeks suggest active policy-related disclosure; I lack detail to take a directional view but the frequency warrants close monitoring.
Two Reg FD disclosures in January amid surging policy uncertainty suggest management is front-running geopolitical exposure communication; staying neutral until content is clearer.
Back-to-back Reg FD filings in mid-January coincide with the start of the EPU spike; without knowing the substance, I cannot lean long but the proactive disclosure is a mild positive for governance.

A single 8.01 Other Events filing on Feb 13 during peak policy uncertainty and rising oil prices raises concern about adverse geopolitical exposure; I lean avoid until the filing content is clarified.
One Reg FD disclosure in early January; limited information but the macro backdrop of surging EPU and rising crude warrants caution on any name with cross-border supply-chain concentration.
Single Reg FD filing late January; insufficient detail to form a geopolitical view but the elevated VIX and EPU environment argues against aggressive positioning.
